March 1967, aitrr the draft finalized by the Marine Engineering and Shipbuilding Sectional Committee had been approved by the Mechanical Engineering Division Council. 0.2 It is necessary to sound the level of various double bottom tanks,. deep tanks and bilges regularly on ships both out at sea and in port. In the case of double bottom t;inks in way of the cargo holds, the sounding pipes have Further, tank sounding devices to be brought up to the uppermost deck. Rules and by the and sounding pipes are covered both by Statutory Classification Society's Rules. 0.3 A guide for s&ction and installation of sounding pipes on board ships is given in Appendix A. 0.4 For the purpose of deciding whether a. .particular requirement of this standard is complied with, the final value, obseryed or calculated, expressing the result of a test, shall be rounded off in a?cordance with IS: 2-1960*. The number of significant places retained in the rounded off value should be the same as that of the specified value in tbis$tandard. 1. APPENDIX

A

(clause 0.3)
GUIDE FOR SELECTION AND INSTALLATION SOUNDING PIPES OF

A-1. Openings of sounding pipes shall be provided with satisfactory arrangements to prevent the free entry of water. A-2.
In all cargo spaces, sounding pipes coal bunkers protection shall be of steel. shall be well protected and in

A-3. Provision shall be made for sounding all tanks and the bilges of those compartments which are not readily accessible.

A-4. A-5.

The soundings shall be taken as near the suction pipes as practicable.

Every fuel oil tank, all tanks forming part of the structure of the ship and all watertight compartments not being part of machinery space shall have sounding pipes.

A-S.

Name plates shall bc affixed to the upper ends of all sounding

pipes. nor

A-9. Sounding pipes shall not terminate in a passenger in any space which is not efficiently ventilated.

or crew space

A-10. In machinery spaces and tunnels where it is not alw;~ys practicnhlr to extend the sounding pipes as mentioned in A-6 short sounding pipes extending to readily accessible positions above the platform may be fitted, provided those to fuel oil and lubricating oil tanks are not situated adjacent to boilers or electric generators or motors, and arc of the self closing type with parallel plugs. A-11. Short sounding pipes to tanks other than oil tanks shall bc fitted with shut-off cocks or with screw caps attached to the pipes by chains.. A-12. in passenge rships, short sounding pipes should be uf;crl nnl\: for souriding coffer dams and double bottom tanks situated in the machinery space and in all cases shall be fitted with self-closing codks. A-13. I%:hen gauge glasses are used for indicating the level of liquid in t nnks containing 1ubricati:lg oil, fuel oil or other inflimmakle liquid, the glasses shall be of heat resisting quality adequately protected from mechanical damage and fitted with self-closing valves at the lower ends and at the top ends when these arc connected to the tanks below the maximum liquid level. A-14. Sounding piprs to oil compartment shall not terminate within refrigerated cargo chambers or in the fan and battery rooms for these chambers, or in enclosed spaces from which access is provided to refrigerated cargo chambers or their fan and battery rooms, when it is practicable. A-15. Where these sounding pipes terminate in such spaces, as mentioned in A-14, they shall be fitted with self closing cocks having parallel plugs. A-16. Sounding pipes shall have a bore not less than 32 mm. All sounding pipes whether for comp:n-tments or tanks, which pass through refrigernted spaces, or the insulation thereof, in which the temperatures contempln.ted arc 0�C or below shall not be less than 65 mm bore. 14

IS: 4010 - 1967 A-17. All pipes which storage of refrigerated pass through chambers intended for the carnage products shall be well insulated. or

A-18. Where such pipes pass through chambers intended for a temperature of 0�C or below they shall also be insulated from the steel structure escept in positions where the temperature of the structure is mainly controlled by the external temperature and will normally be above freezing point. P`ipes passing through a deck plate within the ship side insulation, where the deck is fully insulated berow and has an insulation ribband on top, shall be attached to the deck plating. A-19. In the case of pipes adjacent to the shell plating, metallic contact between the pipes and the shell plating or frames shall be arranged as far as practicable. A-20. Elbow sounding pipes shall not be used for deer tanks unless the elbows and pipes are situated within closed coffer dams or within tanks containing similar liquids. A-21. Elbow may, however, be fitted to other tanks and may be used for sounding bilges, provided it is not practicable to lead them direct to the tanks or compartments. A-22. A-23. The elbows shall be of heavy construction In passenger ships, elbow sounding pipes and adequately supported.

shall not be used.
